sources.entry: Telegram Media Downloader | Self-hosted daemon that automatically downloads media from Telegram channels, groups, and forum topics. Docker-native with multi-arch support.

summary.one_liner: A self-hosted Docker daemon that automatically downloads media from Telegram channels, groups, and forum topics based on configurable filters.
summary.what_it_does:
Monitors configured Telegram sources (public and private channels, groups, supergroups, forum topics, and private chats) and downloads new media as it is posted. Downloads can be filtered by file extension, size, date range, and filename pattern, and are organized into per-source folders or a flat directory. Duplicate detection and persistent download tracking mean files are not re-fetched after being moved or renamed. A daemon mode runs checks at a configurable interval, with optional active-hour windows and an aggregate download speed cap. Users can run a post-download command (without a shell) for each file, and send Discord webhook or generic HTTP POST notifications when downloads complete. Configuration is entirely through environment variables with the TDL_ prefix.</whatitdoes>
<parameter name="how_to_run">["mkdir telegram-downloader && cd telegram-downloader", "Create docker-compose.yml with image rfsbraz/telegram-downloader:latest and TDL_API_ID, TDL_API_HASH, TDL_PHONE_NUMBER, TDL_DAEMON_ENABLED=true, TDL_SOURCES_0_URL set", "docker compose run --rm telegram-downloader (enter the Telegram verification code when prompted)", "docker compose up -d (daemon mode after authentication)"]
use_cases: Automatically download new files posted in Telegram channels
Archive ebooks from a Telegram forum topic
Mirror or back up media from Telegram groups to a home server
Run a Telegram downloader on a Raspberry Pi or ARM server
Trigger extraction or library scans after each download
how_to_run: Create docker-compose.yml with image rfsbraz/telegram-downloader:latest and TDL_API_ID, TDL_API_HASH, TDL_PHONE_NUMBER, TDL_DAEMON_ENABLED=true, TDL_SOURCES_0_URL set
docker compose run --rm telegram-downloader (enter the Telegram verification code when prompted)
docker compose up -d (daemon mode after authentication)
notable: Persistent download tracking so files are not re-downloaded after being moved or renamed
Post-download hook with placeholders like {file}, {dir}, {source}, run without a shell
Active-hours scheduling and aggregate bandwidth cap via MAX_DOWNLOAD_SPEED
Multi-arch Docker images (amd64/arm64) with health checks and non-root user
Migration guide from telegram-download-daemon with settings map
caveats: Requires Telegram API credentials from my.telegram.org and an account with access to the target chats
Initial setup needs interactive login with a verification code sent to your phone
Telegram rate limits (FloodWait) can slow downloads; the daemon waits automatically
Expired or revoked sessions require deleting the session file and re-authenticating
